title: Refactor kernel adapter layer to support simultaneous CUTLASS versions and staged CUDA/Triton upgrades
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Multiple downstream customers and internal clusters currently require different CUTLASS versions (2.x for legacy F32 kernels, 3.x for new int8/quantized paths). We also need to migrate builders from CUDA 11.8 -> 12.x and Triton runtime 2.x -> 3.x. The current codebase assumes a single CUTLASS compile target which blocks incremental rollouts and causes frequent CI breakage when experimental CUTLASS or CUDA changes land.

Goal: Refactor the kernel adapter layer so that we can build and ship multiple CUTLASS-backed kernel variants from the same codebase, add runtime variant selection, and create a predictable CI/build matrix for CUDA/Triton combinations. This will enable staged upgrades (canary on a subset of models/hosts) and reduce churn when upgrading third-party dependency stacks.
acceptance_criteria: Add an adapter abstraction that is unit-testable and separates allocator/stream/cublas handles from CUTLASS-specific includes and templates.
Repository can produce artifacts for CUTLASS-2.x and CUTLASS-3.x kernels via separate build targets (two binaries or a single binary with plugin blobs).
CI matrix includes CUDA 11.8 / CUDA 12.1 and Triton 2.3 / Triton 3.0 combinations and runs representative microbenchmarks.
Runtime selects kernel variant based on model metadata and env config without requiring a full redeploy.
Performance parity: legacy F32 kernels remain within 5% of baseline; new quantized paths show expected speedups in microbench harness.
Rollout plan documented with canary gating metrics and rollback steps.
steps: Design the adapter API and create a short design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Kernel+Adapter+Design
Introduce cmake options CUTLASS_VERSION and TRITON_COMPAT to toggle build targets
Split kernel sources into adapter/implementation directories and add thin shim headers for CUTLASS-2/3
Add runtime selection: environment variable + model manifest flag + per-host routing policy
Add GitHub Actions matrix jobs (cuda: [11.8,12.1], triton: [2.3,3.0], cutlass: [2,3]) with limited microbenchmarks to keep CI time reasonable
Run performance sweep on internal perf cluster and capture results in a dedicated dashboard
Ship canary to 5% of requests on prod-dedicated pool, monitor latency, p99, error rate and model quality regressions
Iterate on fixes and expand rollout to 50% then 100% if metrics are green
comments: 2025-02-19 - Ava Martinez: Kicked off design review. Initial draft linked in steps. Asked infra to reserve two 80GB A100 nodes for perf runs.
2025-02-25 - Julian Park: Created branch 'multi-cutlass-adapters' and pushed initial adapter skeleton, see PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3456
2025-02-27 - Priya Rao (SRE): Confirmed CI runners for CUDA 12.1 are available in the 'cuda-upgrades' pool. Noted that GPU images need libcudnn pinned to 8.4 for Triton 3.0 tests.
2025-03-02 - Design review: Agreement to use a plugin-like build target to avoid doubling production binary size. Decided to maintain separate symbol prefixes to avoid accidental ODR across variants.
2025-03-04 - Julian Park: Added GH Actions matrix and reduced microbench set to 4 kernels to keep job time under 45m. Perf runs scheduled for 2025-03-06.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: CUTLASS API differences may require non-trivial code divergence. Mitigation: Keep adapter surface intentionally small and write compatibility shims that translate our allocator/stream wrapper to CUTLASS expectations.
Risk: CI runtime explosion. Mitigation: limit matrix permutations in PR checks and run full matrix only on main branch nightly builds.
Risk: Performance regression for legacy models. Mitigation: baseline microbenchmarks and per-model golden prompts for output fidelity checks prior to canary rollout.
Risk: Triton ABI changes. Mitigation: pin compatible Triton releases and add integration tests that exercise the Triton plugin loading path.
Risk: Image size and memory footprint. Mitigation: use dynamic plugin blobs and loader logic to keep resident memory low; measure before rollout.
